correctness.rationale: The exact weighted derivative at a maximal/minimal pair decomposes into direct-edge and common-neighbor contributions plus nonpositive exclusive terms. Concavity/strict convexity solves the common-neighbor minimization at every p>1. The Dini maximum formula gives the universal bound. Explicit minimizing-pair values make every contribution exact, proving the optimal coefficient even with tied extrema. Scalar comparison, finite diameter equivalence and logarithmic two-weight limit prove the ancillary claims. The included checker passed 490 exact sharpness witnesses, 3920 exact differential tests, 27475 finite topology instances and 1750 real-power diagnostics; those tests corroborate but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: A naturally motivated sharp functional-analytic dissipation invariant is evaluated for every finite symmetric weighted graph with arbitrary positive vertex masses, conductances and p>1. The all-graph exact coefficient and its equality configurations yield a quantitative consensus estimate; the p>2 power-mean term and complete-versus-noncomplete high-p dichotomy reveal a genuine nonlinear structural transition. Unlike a narrow recomputation of p=2 or a single graph example, the result evaluates an optimal invariant on an infinite, structurally varied class.
